topics.title: 教育·选专业
topics.prompt: Some people believe university students should study whatever they like. Others think they should only study subjects that will be useful. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

arguments.point: Interest drives sustained effort.
arguments.explain: Students who choose subjects they genuinely enjoy are far more likely to study consistently and go beyond the syllabus on their own.
arguments.example: A friend who loved design spent evenings learning software voluntarily and built a strong portfolio before graduating.

arguments.point: Practical subjects improve employability.
arguments.explain: Fields such as engineering, medicine and computer science give graduates concrete skills that employers can immediately use.
arguments.example: In many countries, graduates in technical disciplines find work within months, while some arts graduates struggle for over a year.

topics.tips: 双观点题：一段支持兴趣（论点+解释+例子），一段支持实用（同上），末段折中：先兴趣、兼顾就业。

topics.title: 健康·运动 vs 饮食
topics.prompt: Some people think that the best way to stay healthy is to do regular exercise. Others believe diet is more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

arguments.point: Exercise strengthens the body in ways diet cannot.
arguments.explain: Regular physical activity improves cardiovascular health, builds muscle and reduces stress — benefits that no food alone can provide.
arguments.example: People who walk briskly for thirty minutes a day show measurably lower rates of heart disease.

arguments.point: Diet is the foundation of health.
arguments.explain: Weight and many chronic conditions are driven mainly by what we eat; a poor diet cannot be out-trained.
arguments.example: Even athletes who train daily struggle with health problems if their diet is high in processed food.

topics.tips: 双观点题：运动段（心血管/肌肉/压力），饮食段（体重/慢性病），末段认为两者互补、缺一不可。

topics.title: 城市化·乡村到城市
topics.prompt: In many countries, people are moving from rural areas to cities. What problems does this cause, and what measures could solve them?

arguments.point: Urbanisation creates housing and infrastructure pressure.
arguments.explain: Rapid population growth in cities outpaces housing supply, pushing rents up and straining transport, schools and hospitals.
arguments.example: Several megacities now have commutes of over an hour each way because transport systems were not built for their current population.

arguments.point: Rural areas lose their workforce.
arguments.explain: When young people leave, farms and local businesses lose labour, and villages face ageing populations and declining services.
arguments.example: In parts of Europe, rural schools close because there are not enough children left.

arguments.point: Solutions include decentralisation and rural investment.
arguments.explain: Governments can move administrative and corporate jobs to regional cities and invest in rural infrastructure and services.
arguments.example: Some countries offer tax breaks to companies that open offices outside capital cities, which has slowed migration.

topics.tips: 问题+措施题：问题两段（城市压力 / 乡村流失），措施一段（分散化+投资），措施要具体。

topics.title: 环境·个人 vs 政府责任
topics.prompt: Some people believe individuals should take responsibility for protecting the environment, while others think governments should take the lead. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

arguments.point: Individual choices add up.
arguments.explain: When millions of people reduce waste, recycle and choose public transport, the combined effect is substantial.
arguments.example: Curbside recycling programmes succeed only because households sort their waste every day.

arguments.point: Governments control the biggest levers.
arguments.explain: Only governments can regulate industry emissions, set environmental standards and fund large-scale clean energy projects.
arguments.example: Air quality in several major cities improved sharply only after governments restricted industrial emissions.

topics.tips: 双观点题：个人段（积少成多+例子），政府段（监管/大项目），末段：两者结合，政府定规则、个人落实。

topics.title: 科技·手机与社交
topics.prompt: In many countries, people spend more time on their phones than with friends and family. What problems does this cause, and how can they be solved?

arguments.point: Smartphones weaken face-to-face relationships.
arguments.explain: Constant screen use reduces the quality of conversations and makes people feel ignored even when physically together.
arguments.example: Many families now eat dinner with everyone looking at their own phone.

arguments.point: Screen time affects sleep and concentration.
arguments.explain: Late-night scrolling delays sleep and leaves people tired and less productive the next day.
arguments.example: Studies link heavy evening phone use with lower academic performance in teenagers.

arguments.point: Solutions include clear rules and digital breaks.
arguments.explain: Households and schools can set screen-free times and zones, while individuals can schedule regular offline periods.
arguments.example: Some schools now collect phones at the start of the day and report better attention in class.

topics.tips: 问题+措施题：两个问题段落 + 一个措施段落（规则/断网时段/学校政策）。

topics.title: 工作·远程办公
topics.prompt: More and more companies allow employees to work from home. Do the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages?

arguments.point: Remote work saves time and money.
arguments.explain: Employees avoid long commutes, and companies can reduce office costs while hiring talent from anywhere.
arguments.example: A worker who saves two hours of commuting each day can reinvest that time in family or exercise.

arguments.point: It can weaken collaboration and onboarding.
arguments.explain: Casual conversations that generate ideas are harder online, and new employees learn more slowly without nearby colleagues.
arguments.example: Many firms report that junior staff need extra mentoring when working fully remotely.

topics.tips: 利弊题：优点段（省时间/成本/招聘范围），缺点段（协作/新人培养），末段给出立场：混合办公最平衡。

topics.title: 教育·大学免费
topics.prompt: Some people think university education should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

arguments.point: Free university widens access.
arguments.explain: When tuition is removed, talented students from low-income families can study without taking on debt.
arguments.example: Countries with tuition-free systems have higher university enrolment among disadvantaged groups.

arguments.point: It may strain public budgets and quality.
arguments.explain: Making university free for all, including wealthy families, is extremely expensive and can force cuts to teaching quality.
arguments.example: Some governments have had to cap student numbers because free tuition became unaffordable.

topics.tips: 同意与否题：支持段（公平/流动性），反对段（财政/质量），末段折中：按收入提供资助而非全民免费。

topics.title: 社会·老龄化
topics.prompt: In many countries, the population is ageing rapidly. What problems does this cause, and what measures could governments take?

arguments.point: Ageing increases pressure on healthcare and pensions.
arguments.explain: A smaller working population must fund the pensions and medical care of a growing number of retirees.
arguments.example: Several countries have had to raise the retirement age to keep pension systems solvent.

arguments.point: Labour shortages slow economic growth.
arguments.explain: Fewer young workers means businesses struggle to fill positions, which can reduce productivity.
arguments.example: Some economies now rely on immigration to fill roles in healthcare and construction.

arguments.point: Measures include later retirement and family support.
arguments.explain: Governments can encourage later retirement, support childcare and invest in automation to offset labour shortages.
arguments.example: Flexible part-time work for older employees keeps experienced staff in the workforce longer.

topics.tips: 问题+措施题：医疗养老压力、劳动力短缺两段，措施段给 2-3 个具体政策。

topics.title: 媒体·事实与观点
topics.prompt: Some people think the media should report only facts, while others believe opinion and analysis are also valuable. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

arguments.point: Facts protect public trust.
arguments.explain: When news is strictly factual, audiences can form their own views without being manipulated by bias.
arguments.example: Outlets that separate news reporting from opinion commentary are generally rated as more trustworthy.

arguments.point: Analysis helps people understand complex issues.
arguments.explain: Raw facts rarely explain causes and consequences; expert analysis turns information into understanding.
arguments.example: During economic crises, analysis helps readers see why prices are rising, not just that they are.

topics.tips: 双观点题：事实段（信任/客观），分析段（理解复杂问题），末段：两者都需要，但必须明确区分。

topics.title: 科技·AI 与就业
topics.prompt: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in the workplace. Do the benefits of this development outweigh the drawbacks?

arguments.point: AI raises productivity and reduces repetitive work.
arguments.explain: Automating routine tasks frees workers to focus on creative and interpersonal work that machines cannot do.
arguments.example: Customer service teams using AI handle routine questions faster and spend more time on complex cases.

arguments.point: It can displace workers and widen inequality.
arguments.explain: Jobs built around predictable tasks are most at risk, and the benefits tend to go to those with capital and advanced skills.
arguments.example: Some factories now need far fewer workers for the same output.

topics.tips: 利弊题：优点段（效率/释放人力），缺点段（岗位替代/不平等），末段：需要再培训与社会保障配套。
